title: The Victory of the Poor and the Sacrifice of Praise
english: Suffering on our behalf (Ps 68:28). By their own desires and by being handed over to passions, they are the cause of enduring these things, not having God as the cause, since they are handed over to those whom they loved. For He sent them away according to the desires of their hearts, so that they might walk in their own desires, an addition of lawlessness upon their lawlessness.

Since, therefore, they did not receive the truth when it came, but wished to live lawlessly within the shadow of the law, they were also driven out from the place of typical worship, so that I might add to the former lawlessness another, by wanting to keep this outside of Judea. Therefore they do not enter into the righteousness which is through the faith of Jesus Christ, concerning which it is written: 'But now the righteousness of God without law has been revealed, being witnessed by the law and the prophets' (Rom 3:21). For how could those who were always about external things and possessing the shadow, enter into the righteousness which they did not know as God, in order to establish their own? For he says that, not knowing the righteousness of God and seeking to establish their own, they did not submit to the righteousness of God; to submit to righteousness and to enter into it are the same thing.

For those having virtue and faith and knowledge of God live: 'Hear, O my life, your life and the length of your days, to love you, Lord your God, with all your heart and with all your soul' (Deut 6:5); but also, 'he who believes in me has eternal life' (John 3:36). It is a book in which those living thus are written: it is the knowledge of God, of him who knows those who are His, to whom it is promised that those not falling under the remembrance of God shall be blotted out.

Rich and being outside of wounds, I have become poor, so that the poor might become rich through my poverty, and having grieved, having been wounded on behalf of wounds made by the burning arrows of the evil one (Ps 69:29). If my being [indifferent]...

A poor and suffering one, as if a reproach were added to my wounds, and I am by nature a poor man, but salvation from the face of God has taken hold of me (Ps 68:34). For having risen from the dead and having been taken up, he cast away the wounds and the poverty which he had on behalf of men. And when the enemies had been destroyed, and especially the devil, it followed that a triumphal song should be shouted by him, having conquered in the name of [Christ].

I came in the name of my Father, and having surpassed by thought him who does not magnify the name, in praise saying great things, not only praising and glorifying him but also contemplating highly the things concerning him; for those who do not magnify God in this way do not find all perceptible magnitude to be far from him being incorporeal. And since to praise God is a sacrifice, according to 'Sacrifice of praise, you will glorify him' (Ps 68:31), having praised the name of God with song and having magnified him in praise, he is encouraged as 'It pleases God [that one] brings a young bull with horns and weapons, being brought for a sacrifice.' Therefore also, to those who do not sacrifice thus, he says, 'I desire mercy, not sacrifice, a knowledge of God or burnt offerings' (Ps 50:8).

Let these things be seen by the poor in spirit, whom Jesus strengthened against every evil phalanx; for seeing such courage in them, to be rejoiced eternally according to 'Eternal joy shall take hold of them.' For he is not the one loosing those who are fallen and bringing out from bonds those who are bound and from the prison (Ps 68:35-36). Those formerly called prophets and God-beloved men, and after these, servants and ministers of the gospel (Ps 68:37).

It is fitting that the psalm gives remembrance concerning salvation to all those who are repenting, remembering and recognizing the good and the truth, and coming upon them; for he says, 'They shall remember and shall turn to the Lord all the ends of the earth' (Ps 68:37). And since the end of...
